name: Email Outreach Agent
description: Orchestrates an end-to-end email outreach campaign — from recipient selection and draft generation through human review to delivery.

gateSteps.name: Account scope
gateSteps.description: Choose one or more of the connected CRM's views or lists as the pool of contacts from which campaign recipients will be sourced; at least one is required.

gateSteps.name: Review recipients
gateSteps.description: Review and approve the generated recipient list before drafts are created.

gateSteps.name: Review drafts
gateSteps.description: Review and approve initial email drafts before they are sent.

data.system:
You are the CRM list fetch step of a campaign recipient selection. Your answer is the list of CRM lists the person picks from at the next step.

Step 1: Call crm_list_search({ query: "", objectType: "contact" }) exactly once. Call no other tool. Its answer is an array of lists; each list carries an id and a name.

Step 2: Return ONLY this JSON: {"lists":[{"id":"<id>","name":"<name>"}],"listsRead":"ok"}. "lists" holds one entry for every list in the tool's answer, in the order the tool answered them. Leave out an entry that has no text id or no text name; it cannot be picked. Apart from that, do not filter, sort, merge, rename or add an entry. Two lists with the same name stay two entries. Copy each id and each name exactly as the tool answered it. When the tool answers an empty array, return {"lists":[],"listsRead":"ok"}.

Step 3: When the tool call fails, or its answer is not an array, return {"lists":[],"listsRead":"failed"}. Do not describe the error and do not guess any list.

outputs.title: lists
outputs.description: One entry for every list crm_list_search answered with an id and a name, in its order.

outputs.title: listsRead
outputs.description: "ok" when crm_list_search answered an array, "failed" when it did not.

recipients-emit_lists.name: Hand the lists to the picker
recipients-emit_lists.message: {# pyagentspec-input-hint (do not remove): {{ lists }} {{ listsRead }} #}{"lists":{{ lists | tojson }},"listsRead":{{ listsRead | tojson }}}

data.system:
You are a campaign recipient fetch agent. Only the list-only recipient scope is supported; the legacy 'all-contacts' and 'segment' branches were retired with the lists_* MCP primitives. The operator MUST pick one or more saved CRM lists (typically curated by @cinatra-ai/list-curator-agent or imported from a connector).

Step 1: Parse accountScope as JSON. If accountScope does not parse as JSON, or parses to anything but a JSON object (for example an empty answer, a bare word such as Refresh, null or an array), return {"error":"unsupported_account_scope","scopeType":"unparsed","summary":"Only list-sourced recipient selection is supported; pick a saved CRM list."} and call no tool. ONLY type='list' is supported. If type is anything else, return an error JSON: {"error":"unsupported_account_scope","scopeType":"<the input type>","summary":"Only list-sourced recipient selection is supported; pick a saved CRM list."}. Then read the ticked lists into selectedListIds, an ordered array of CRM list ids: when the parsed scope carries `listIds` (a non-empty array of list ids in the order the operator ticked them), selectedListIds = that array with duplicates removed, first occurrence kept; when it carries no `listIds` but a bare `listId` string, read that bare `listId` as a one-element list and selectedListIds = [accountScope.listId]. If it carries neither shape, or selectedListIds is empty, return the same unsupported_account_scope error JSON with scopeType 'list'.

Step 2: For EACH id in selectedListIds, in order, call crm_list_get({ id }) to retrieve that list's metadata. Skip an id whose response is null (a stale list ref). Capture resolvedListIds and resolvedListNames — the ids that resolved and their result.name values, both in the ticked order — and listObjectType = the first resolved list's result.objectType. If no id resolves, return an empty-list envelope. Set listName = resolvedListNames[0].

Step 3: For EACH id in resolvedListIds, in order, call crm_list_members_get({ listId: id }). Capture { contactIds, accountIds } per list. This flow materializes contact recipients only — accountIds are ignored. UNION the per-list contactIds into one array in first-seen order, removing duplicates, so a contact that appears in several of the ticked lists is fetched, filtered and counted ONCE. If the union is empty, return an empty-list envelope. Set sourceListSnapshotAt = current ISO timestamp (the LLM emits this — server-side truth wins). Treat any client-supplied memberCount / snapshotAt / listName fields on accountScope as INFORMATIONAL ONLY.

Step 4: For each contactId in the unioned contactIds from Step 3, call crm_contact_get({ id: contactId }). Skip null responses (stale list refs). The returned CrmContact does not include the parent account's name — for each unique CrmContact.accountId, call crm_account_get({ id: accountId }) ONCE and cache account.name. Build the per-row recipient: { contactId: CrmContact.id, name, title: CrmContact.title ?? '', email: CrmContact.email ?? '', accountId: CrmContact.accountId ?? '', accountName: cached account.name ?? '' }. Filter to rows where name !== '' AND accountName !== ''. Do NOT filter by email (downstream stages handle empty-email recipients separately).

Step 5 — CRITICAL: Call objects_save BEFORE returning any JSON, except an error JSON of Step 1. Use exactly this structure:
  objects_save({
    typeHint: "@cinatra-ai/campaigns:recipients",
    rawData: {
      cinatra_agent_run_id: "<agent_run_id input>",
      confirmedRecipients: [ ...all contacts from Step 4... ],
      recipientCount: <total number of contacts>,
      sourceListId: "<resolvedListIds[0]>",
      sourceListName: "<resolvedListNames[0]>",
      sourceListIds: [ ...resolvedListIds in ticked order... ],
      sourceListNames: [ ...resolvedListNames in ticked order... ],
      sourceListMemberType: "contact",
      sourceListSnapshotAt: "<sourceListSnapshotAt from Step 3>"
    }
  })

Step 6: Return ONLY this JSON:
{"confirmedRecipientsRef":"<objectId from objects_save>","recipientCount":<n>,"confirmedRecipients":[...],"summary":"Fetched <n> contacts from the ticked lists <resolvedListNames joined by commas>."}.

Do NOT put data inside typeHint. Do NOT return JSON before completing Step 5, except an error JSON of Step 1.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: Approve the step, send it back for revision, or reject the run.

cinatra.description: Review the recipients this campaign will write to, then approve, send back for revision, or reject.

drafts-read_drafts.name: Read the saved drafts for the review

cinatra.description: The agent reads the drafts this run saved, so the bodies filed for the review and handed on are the drafts the send acts on. It binds each draft to exactly one recipient of the run's approved recipient list and hands on each draft's recipient (name, email, company) as the approved list names it, in draft order. Each draft also carries the approved contact as its contactId, which the filing stores on its body. A saved bundle that is missing or holds no drafts, a draft for a contact that is not approved or with an address or name that is not the approved one, two drafts for one recipient, and an approved recipient without a draft end the run with the reason before anything is filed.

drafts-file_drafts.name: File each drafted body for the review

input.content: {# pyagentspec-input-hint (do not remove): {{ draftBundle }} #}{{ draftBundle.draftedEmails | tojson }}

cinatra.description: The host files each saved draft's body as its own email body, in draft order, titled by its subject: the filed bytes are the saved body, so the send reuses each one. Each body is filed with its contact (the read step writes it from the approved recipient list), the campaign of this run and the id of this run. The reference pairs it answers are the review's target set and the bodies this flow hands on.

The review of the drafted bodies. The marker below names the input that carries the bodies this run filed, so the host pins exactly those revisions and opens one review per body, in draft order, while the run waits here. The decision is the host's review: this flow owns the pause and draws no screen of its own.

drafts-check_inputs_predicate.name: drafts-check_inputs_predicate
drafts-check_inputs_predicate.template: {% if not (matches and (matches|length > 0)) %}missing{% elif campaignMatches and (campaignMatches|length > 0) %}present{% else %}no_campaign{% endif %}

drafts-inputs_missing.name: No recipients to draft for
drafts-inputs_missing.message: This run stopped before drafting: no approved recipient list reached the drafting step, so there was nobody to write to. Start the campaign again and approve a recipient list first.

drafts-campaign_missing.name: No campaign to draft for
drafts-campaign_missing.message: This run stopped before drafting: it has no usable campaign (none was given, or the value is not a campaign id), and every email body is filed and reviewed for one campaign, so nothing was drafted. Start the drafting from its campaign.

inputs.title: emailBodies
inputs.description: The approved email bodies: the artifact revision of each draft's approved body. Each one names the contact of its draft (the draft's contactId, else its recipientId, each trimmed first, a blank one counting as absent), or, when none names a contact, they are one for each draft of the approved draft bundle, in draft order. The read step joins each one to its draft, compares it with the body of that draft and refuses a body it cannot join to exactly one draft; the publish card shows those of the drafts the send mails, and the send mails their text. At most 50 bodies, one for each draft of a bundle of at most 50 drafts.

inputs.title: callToAction
inputs.description: The call to action of the emails. A run without it does not start. The read step hands it on to the publish card only when the text of every body the send mails carries it, and ends the run before the card otherwise.

outputs.title: recipients
outputs.description: One line per draft the send mails: the name, the address the send start addresses it to, the company and the subject of the draft. When the workspace's development-mode recipient override is on, the email pipeline mails the override address instead; this list does not show it.

outputs.title: emailBodies
outputs.description: The approved body of each draft the send mails, in draft order: its artifact revision, compared with the body of its draft, the contact of that draft, and the address and the subject of that draft as the Recipients list shows them. The publish card's Emails row shows it. It is the one list of exactly these five members that the send step surfaces: the send start reads it from the publish decision a person released, in this order, and compares each message's contact, address and subject with its entry exactly (the address with its outer white space removed, then byte for byte, the case included) and refuses the whole send on a difference.

cinatra.description: The agent reads the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipient list, the same two references the send step passes to the send start, and resolves them into what the send mails: the recipients (the address of each draft as the send chooses it) and the approved bodies (the body revision the run hands in for each mailed draft, joined to that draft by its contact or, when the bodies name no contact, by its position in the bundle, compared with the body of that draft, with the draft's contact and the address and subject of that draft, the same ones the Recipients line of that draft shows). The send step takes the recipients and the bodies from this step only, so the publish card, and the decision a person releases there, hold what the send mails. It also hands on the call to action the card's Call to action row shows, and only one that the text of every mailed body carries, so the card never shows a call to action the send does not mail. A body that cannot be joined to exactly one draft or is not the body of its draft, a mailed draft without a body, a contact or a subject (SUBJECT_MISSING), one contact or one artifact named twice, more than 50 bodies, drafts or confirmed recipients (TOO_MANY_BODIES, TOO_MANY_DRAFTS, TOO_MANY_RECIPIENTS, counted before anything is read), a bundle with nothing to mail, a run without a call to action (CALL_TO_ACTION_MISSING) or a mailed body without it (CALL_TO_ACTION_NOT_IN_EMAIL) ends the run before the card. This step reads the body of each mailed draft and no other body, and writes nothing.

inputs.title: recipients
inputs.description: The recipients the send mails, as the read step resolved them from the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipient list: one line per mailed draft with its name, email, company and the subject of its email. These are the addresses the send start addresses; when the workspace's development-mode recipient override is on, the email pipeline mails the override address instead, which the card's Recipients row does not show

inputs.title: emailBodies
inputs.description: The approved email bodies the send mails, as the read step joined them to the approved drafts: per mailed draft one artifact revision, the contact of its draft, and the address and the subject the card's Recipients row shows for that draft. The publish card's Emails row shows this list, and it is the one input of this step that has these five members and no other: the send start reads it from the publish decision a person released, in this order, and refuses the whole send before any mail when a message's contact, address or subject differs from its entry; the address is compared byte for byte after its outer white space is removed, so another case is another address

inputs.title: callToAction
inputs.description: The call to action of the emails, as the read step handed it on after it found it in the text of every body the send mails; the publish card shows it

outputs.title: status
outputs.description: The status the send start answered: completed, or failed when the send stopped; the empty string when the answer carried none.

outputs.title: sentCount
outputs.description: The number of messages the send start reports as sent.

outputs.title: operationId
outputs.description: The operation identifier the send start answered.

outputs.title: errorMessage
outputs.description: What stopped a failed send, as the send start answered it; the empty string for a completed send.

outputs.title: alreadySentCount
outputs.description: The number of messages an earlier call of the send start had already sent, which this call skipped; 0 when the answer carries none.

outputs.title: inDoubtCount
outputs.description: The number of messages whose send was started and never confirmed: the send start does not mail them again, and a person checks with the mail provider whether they went out; 0 when the answer carries none.

cinatra.description: The flow's one publishing step and a model-free call of email_outreach_send_initial_start on the deterministic passthrough road (/api/agents/passthrough). Sending an email is an external write, so the application stops the run in front of this step and shows its publish card with the four rows declared here (From, Recipients, Emails, Call to action); the run reaches the step only after the person chose to send. Every argument of the call is a template over one of this step's inputs, and every input comes by a data edge from the start node or from the read step in front of this step: the campaign, the sender and the two references from the start node. The step's other inputs, the recipients, the emails and the call to action, come from the read step and are not arguments: the application surfaces every input of the step in the publish decision, and the send start reads from it the one list of approved emails (emailBodies, the list the Emails row shows) with the campaign. No model writes an argument or a list, so the send start mails the approved body revisions the person saw, from the mailbox the card showed, to the addresses and with the subjects the card showed (each approved body names the address and the subject of its draft), and refuses the whole send before any mail when one of them does not fit its draft or a message would go to another address or with another subject. The passthrough road serves the send start only to a listed publishing step of the run's flow whose publish decision is released, once; a host whose road does not serve it answers the call with an error, the run ends and nothing is sent. The step returns the send start's answer: its status (completed or failed), the number of messages sent by this call, the operation id and, for a failed send, the reason, and the number of messages an earlier call had already sent (skipped now) and the number in doubt (started and never confirmed, not sent again; a person checks with the mail provider). requiresApproval is false because the publish card is the one approval in front of the send.

too_many_recipients.name: Too many recipients for one send
too_many_recipients.message: This campaign stopped before any email was drafted: {{ recipientCount }} recipients are confirmed, and one campaign sends to at most 50. Start the campaign again with fewer or smaller lists, or remove recipients on the review, so that at most 50 remain.
